episode.episode: Philips Hue: The smart home’s light bulb moment
episode.showDescription: Version History is a show about the best gadgets ever. And the worst ones. And the ones that might have changed the world, if they ever actually shipped. Every week, your favorite people from The Verge and beyond hang out to tell and debate the story of a gadget, app, website, or any other tech product, and try to determine the item’s true legacy. Because not every product is a hit, but every product has a story. And the ones that really matter aren’t always the ones you think. From the Verge and the Vox Media Podcast Network.
episode.episodeDescription: The humble light bulb might be the ultimate success story in the smart home. Our connected, adaptable homes are supposed to be customizable, connected to everything, and incredibly easy to use, and nothing has made that work quite like Philips Hue lights. In this episode, The Verge's David Pierce and Jennifer Pattison Tuohy are joined by smart home journalist and expert Richard Gunther to tell the Hue's story. We trace the product's history from its origins in the smartphone revolution, try to figure out how Philips managed to turn a staggeringly expensive lightbulb into a must-have gadget, and look at whether there's even more invention left in the future of lighting. transcript_window.text: They're basically just, it was a round piece of plastic and then it was a rectangle piece of plastic.
And this was the thing that plugged into your router that actually connected the whole network.
And that's how then the bulbs connected to it over the Zigbee protocol and you were able to control your lights with your phone.
It was all, it was the heart of the system.
Bring back the round one, Phyllis.
But so the reason they had to stop, the reason they were late, they decided really importantly at the last minute was we need to make these bulbs upgradable.
Up until that point, the idea was just the bridge could create new features.
And through the app, you could have new features for the bridge.
But they decided, OK, we're going to strip out all the features we've tried to cram in here and we're to make it upgradable.
so that we can do it right as we go along rather than trying.
So that they can actually upgrade the bulb and not just the bridge.
